nodes.content: Design a stateful edge proxy that preserves established TCP sessions across anycast rerouting and single-site failures.
requirements: Preserve byte ordering and acknowledged data without endpoint changes, including failures during connection-state migration.
Keep p99 application-visible failover stalls below 500 milliseconds with 50-millisecond intersite RTT.

nodes.content: Synchronously mirror both TCP legs’ sequence state and payload before ACK; prewarm a movable-tuple backup for BFD-triggered, epoch-fenced takeover.
How does takeover avoid losing ACKed bytes or duplicating delivery if the active site crashes during state migration?
Under mid-migration crashes, quorum-committed payload and sequence checkpoints with epoch-fenced replay yield zero ACKed-byte loss or duplicate delivery.
Implement ACK-gated journaling and epoch-fenced takeover; inject checkpoint-boundary crashes at 50-ms RTT, measuring byte loss, duplicates, and p99 stalls.
Run CrashBoundary-50 at 50-ms RTT: kill primaries across commit phases on 10,000 streams; measure loss, duplicates, p99 stalls.
CrashBoundary-50 found duplicated backend delivery in 11/10,000 streams when independently committed TCP-leg checkpoints straddled a crash.
Atomic cross-leg write-ahead records before ACK or backend send, with fenced same-tuple replay, prevent ACKed-byte loss and duplicate delivery.
Implement atomic cross-leg WAL; rerun CrashBoundary-50’s 11 duplicate cases plus phase-boundary kills, measuring ACKed-byte loss, backend duplicates, and p99 stalls.
CrashBoundary-50 retest: zero ACKed-byte loss or duplicate backend delivery across 10,000 streams; p99 stall 340 ms.
Adopt atomic cross-leg WAL over independent checkpoints: it eliminated the 11 duplicate cases while keeping p99 stalls at 340 ms.
Run AnycastFlip-50 with atomic WAL at 50-ms RTT; withdraw active-site routes, checking tuple continuity, ordered delivery, and p99 stalls.
AnycastFlip-50 report contains route-withdrawal traces, unchanged endpoint tuples, zero reordered bytes, and 410-ms p99 application-visible stalls.
Can epoch fencing exclude a stale primary while asymmetric anycast convergence sends packets to both sites?
Replay AnycastFlip-50 traces with 200-ms split-route convergence; test epoch fencing for stale-primary forwards, duplicate bytes, and p99 stalls.
With 200-ms split-route convergence, stale primaries forwarded 14 packets after takeover; p99 stalls reached 570 ms, exceeding 500 ms.
Can synchronous mirroring keep failover p99 below 500 ms when transient intersite congestion builds a replication backlog?
ACK-gated replication with a 64-KiB per-flow WAL cap keeps p99 failover stalls below 500 ms during 100-ms congestion bursts.
Inject 100-ms intersite congestion into AnycastFlip-50 route traces with 64-KiB WAL caps; measure p99 stalls, ACKed-byte loss, and duplicates.
With 100-ms congestion bursts and 64-KiB WAL caps, AnycastFlip-50 recorded 460-ms p99 stalls, zero ACKed-byte loss, and zero duplicates.
Keep 64-KiB ACK-gated WAL for 460-ms p99; require backend epoch fencing and stale-site redirection to address split-route forwarding.
Add quorum-leased ownership and an epoch-fenced backend gateway; tunnel split-route packets to the owner while atomic WAL preserves TCP state.
Can quorum-leased ownership fence an isolated primary during split-route convergence without pushing p99 failover stalls above 500 ms?
Implement gateway-enforced lease epochs and stale-site tunneling; inject 200-ms split routes and primary isolation, measuring stale forwards and p99 stalls.
Run LeaseSplit-50: isolate primaries during 200-ms split routes; audit gateway epoch rejects, tunneled packets, and p99 application stalls.
LeaseSplit-50 recorded zero stale backend forwards, but quorum lease expiry delayed takeover, yielding 620-ms p99 application stalls.
Retain gateway epoch fencing but reject expiry-gated takeover: its 620-ms p99 exceeds 500 ms; investigate faster fenced handoff.
BFD-triggered quorum CAS revokes ownership and fences backend gateways before granting standby replay, avoiding lease-expiry waits.
Under 200-ms split routes, quorum CAS with gateway-acknowledged fencing yields zero stale backend forwards and p99 stalls below 500 ms.
Rerun LeaseSplit-50’s 200-ms split routes with BFD-triggered quorum CAS and gateway-acknowledged fencing; measure stale forwards and p99 stalls.
LeaseSplit-50 CAS rerun recorded zero stale backend forwards across 10,000 streams and 430-ms p99 stalls under 200-ms split routes.
Can quorum CAS complete takeover within 500 ms if its coordinator crashes after gateway fencing but before standby grant?
Inject post-fence, pre-grant coordinator crashes in LeaseSplit-50 under 200-ms split routes; measure p99 stalls and stale forwards.
Post-fence coordinator crashes caused zero stale forwards but 780-ms p99 stalls while standbys awaited an orphaned grant.
Standbys use quorum-persisted gateway-fence acknowledgments for idempotent CAS grants after coordinator crashes, yielding zero stale forwards and sub-500-ms p99 stalls.
Rerun post-fence coordinator kills with persisted fence acknowledgments and standby CAS retries; record stale forwards and p99 takeover stalls.
LeaseSplit-50 coordinator-kill rerun recorded zero stale forwards and 455-ms p99 stalls across 10,000 post-fence failures.
Adopt recoverable CAS grants: baseline stalls were 430 ms, coordinator crashes raised them to 780 ms, retries restored 455 ms.
Use a per-session overlay anchor with hot-standby TCP replicas, routing rerouted packets to the quorum-elected owner.
How can a failed overlay anchor be replaced without losing ACKed bytes or exceeding 500-ms p99 application stalls?
Prepublish dual-anchor mappings and replicate atomic WAL; kill anchors at 50-ms RTT, measuring ACKed-byte loss and p99 stalls.
Run AnchorKill-50 on 10,000 streams: kill primary anchors during WAL migration at 50-ms RTT; measure ACKed-byte loss and p99 stalls.
AnchorKill-50 report logs zero ACKed-byte loss across 10,000 streams and 485-ms p99 stalls during anchor replacement.
Repeat AnchorKill-50 with cold standby mapping caches after primary-site loss; compare ACKed-byte loss and p99 stalls to 485-ms baseline.
Cold-cache AnchorKill-50 recorded zero ACKed-byte loss and 492-ms p99 stalls across 10,000 streams, within the 500-ms target.
Keep dual-anchor mapping as fallback: cold-cache p99 reached 492 ms with zero ACKed-byte loss, leaving only 8 ms margin.
Adopt 64-KiB atomic ACK-gated WAL, recoverable quorum-CAS gateway fencing and stale-site tunneling; retain dual-anchor fallback, reject lease-expiry takeover.
